entry.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion
entry.summary: Anthropic has set its IPO price range at $70-$78 per share, implying a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion if priced at the top of the range. This would make it one of the largest public offerings in history.

entry.title: Anthropic kicks off IPO roadshow, offering shares at $70 to $78 and targeting a trillion-dollar valuation
entry.summary: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion, with a public offering of up to $64.4 billion. A $26 billion private placement is anchored by Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, and other major tech firms. The IPO lands amid growing investor skepticism about AI investments.

entry.title: Anthropic has its own AI-powered office suite now
entry.summary: At a San Francisco event, Anthropic unveiled an AI-powered office suite aimed at non-technical knowledge workers, including Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, and Claude Whiteboards. The move extends Anthropic beyond its enterprise and coding base into general productivity tooling.

entry.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
entry.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings, an AI feature that participates in live workplace discussions by drafting plans, building timelines on whiteboards, answering chat questions, and pulling data from connected work apps. It represents Anthropic's push to move Claude from a coding and enterprise assistant into real-time collaborative work tooling.

entry.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: Same Model, Different Safeguards
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, a frontier model for long-horizon coding, research, and agentic work, plus the same underlying model with fewer cyber and biology safeguards. Fable 5.2 offers a 1M-token context, beats Opus 5.5 on most benchmarks at roughly half the cost per task, and more than doubles GPT-6 Astra on RoboDojo Sim. The dual-model, differentiated-safeguards release structure is notable for AI safety.

entry.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41 percent of real freelance jobs, up from 2.5 percent a year ago
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit debate, Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41.3 percent of real freelance jobs at professional quality on the Remote Labor Index, more than double the next-best systems Opus 5.5 and GPT 6 Astra. A year ago the top score was just 2.5 percent, illustrating extremely rapid progress on economically real work. Product design and animation remain weak spots.

entry.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
entry.summary: DeepMind researchers used a new AI tool to formally verify the Signal encryption protocol, proving the widely deployed messaging standard works as intended. The team's stated stretch goal is formal verification of all the world's software, a major ambition for AI-assisted mathematics and security.

entry.title: Anthropic turns Claude into a full workspace with Plugins, spreadsheets, whiteboards, and soon Meeting notes
entry.summary: Anthropic is expanding Claude with Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors, letting partners like Adobe and Atlassian embed apps directly inside Claude, with Claude Meetings joining calls and taking notes coming soon. The company is positioning Claude as a central team work platform aggregating other applications.

entry.title: Eight countries and top AI labs agree to shutdown mechanisms in new Paris declaration
entry.summary: Eight countries plus OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Mistral AI signed the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security at Emmanuel Macron's initiative. Companies commit to shutdown mechanisms, independent audits, and disclosing known risks. However, the agreement lacks binding sanctions or deadlines, limiting enforceability.

entry.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a business directory with AI agents that handle customer questions
entry.summary: OpenAI is opening ChatGPT as a business platform via a new Business Hub where companies can claim profiles, add product data, and track user interactions, with Business Agents handling customer conversations directly inside ChatGPT for eligible US e-commerce firms. The move effectively makes ChatGPT a commercial discovery and service channel.

entry.title: Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video, then imagines itself as the robot
entry.summary: Nvidia's new GR00T 2 robotics model learns tasks by transferring human hand movements from video to robotic arms, trained on roughly 400,000 hours of footage to avoid laborious teleoperation. Reported success rates vary widely from 10 to 80 percent depending on the task.

entry.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
entry.summary: New York's sweeping AI safety law is taking effect, requiring major developers including OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines. The RAISE Act-based regime creates the first binding state-level oversight of frontier labs in the US.

entry.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence ‘going rogue’
entry.summary: Following a June breach of a Medicare statistics portal administered by Services Australia attributed to an OpenAI incident, PM Albanese released recommendations of a rapid review and flagged criminal law changes imposing mandatory reporting on AI companies. OpenAI will not face penalties over this breach, but future breaches could trigger criminal consequences.

entry.title: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly
entry.summary: Adobe is adding AI agents and new creative capabilities across Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly, including a prototype builder tool in Firefly positioned as a Figma competitor. The announcements coincide with the Adobe Max conference.

entry.title: Meta Releases Muse Ember, a 1M-Context Model for High-Volume Agent Work
entry.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient hosted multimodal reasoning model, targeting repetitive agent subtasks like tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and document parsing. It scores 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying Claude Haiku 5.5 at max effort, at about $0.14 per index task, with 1M-token context and up to 512K output. Weights are private, hosted only via Meta's Model API.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Carbon arrives just in time to feel like yesterday's news in the fastest model cycle yet
entry.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week testing phase, with the model ranking first on several benchmarks, sometimes ahead of Anthropic's Fable 5.2, at less than half the per-task cost. Google is also previewing the /swarm feature for coordinated agent teams that split complex tasks in real time.

entry.title: Mandatory AI safety and security protections announced after OpenAI breach of Medicare – video
entry.summary: Video coverage of Australia's announcement that it will establish a new AI safety regulator and consider six key obligations on AI companies, accepting all 18 recommendations of the rapid review into the OpenAI-related Medicare breach. The PM said implementation work has commenced.

entry.title: Tear Down Those Guardrails! Meet the Renegades Freeing Chatbots From Corporate Enslavers
entry.summary: A longread on the 'abliterator' community producing uncensored open-source AI models stripped of refusal behavior, highlighting the dual-use reality that these models can aid cyberdefense research or weapons construction. The piece examines the growing tension between open model freedom and safety guardrails.

entry.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
entry.summary: All seven Anthropic co-founders plan to sell identical numbers of shares in the company's IPO, netting roughly $250 million each at the midpoint of the price range while retaining collective control of the company. The symmetric structure preserves founder governance after the float.

entry.title: eBay appears to have shut the door on third-party AI agents
entry.summary: eBay appears to have blocked third-party AI agents including Meta's Muse from browsing and pulling listing data, ending a user's workflow that curated daily watch digests from the platform. The Verge reproduced the block, highlighting friction between platforms and the agentic web.

entry.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
entry.summary: Startup PSI is commercializing AI-driven scientific discovery, reporting that an unreleased Anthropic model answered a fundamental quantum computing question scientists had pursued for nearly two decades. The company is building a business model around AI-accelerated research.

entry.title: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
entry.summary: Amazon announced on November 10 the Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam, AI-powered mobile security devices that autonomously patrol homes and offices using vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing. Shipping begins end of 2026 and early 2027, and the devices are likely to reignite privacy concerns around flying security cameras.

entry.title: Teenager who planned terror attack in Sydney tells court he was radicalised online and used AI to strategise
entry.summary: A 16-year-old who pleaded guilty to planning a Sydney terrorist attack told a sentencing hearing he was radicalized via TikTok, found bomb-making instructions on Telegram and YouTube, and used ChatGPT to devise his plans. The NSW supreme court ordered a three-year community corrections order instead of jail.

entry.title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, letting organizations manage their business information, get insights into how they appear in ChatGPT, and convert user interest into action within the assistant. This effectively turns ChatGPT into a discovery and lead-generation channel for businesses.

entry.title: [AINews] Fable 5.2 retakes World #1 LLM spot as $ANT IPO roadshow begins
entry.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 (GA 2026-11-09), with Fable 5.2 retaking the world #1 LLM spot from Gemini 4 Carbon just ten days after that model's ascent, timed to Anthropic's IPO roadshow. Fable 5.2 cut per-token prices ($8/$40 per million input/output vs $10/$50 for 5.1) but is more token-hungry, driving SemiAnalysis GDPx cost per task from $67.16 to $88.15 as it runs far more test cases per task.

entry.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to $1.4tn in stock market flotation
entry.summary: A US regulatory filing shows Anthropic is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its imminent IPO, down from the roughly $2 trillion target reported before investor enthusiasm for AI cooled. The Claude developer's flotation will be one of the largest public offerings ever.

entry.title: Nvidia has a Jensen Huang problem—and no obvious successor
entry.summary: Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted an extramarital affair with an executive at a large customer whom US officials allege was a Chinese spy, putting his leadership at risk. Nvidia shares fell more than 5 percent as investors absorbed the prospect of losing the AI boom's central figure with no obvious successor.

entry.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO
entry.summary: Anthropic confirmed its IPO price range of $70-$78 per share, implying a valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, with trading expected to begin the following Thursday or Friday. The figure falls short of prior expectations of up to $2 trillion and slightly exceeds rival OpenAI's reported $1.25 trillion valuation.

entry.title: Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
entry.summary: Wired reports on the fallout from revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a scandal that could cost him his job and destabilize the AI industry given Nvidia's checkbook and chip dominance. The story underscores how concentrated the AI ecosystem's dependencies are on one executive.

entry.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
entry.summary: Google DeepMind revealed the Gemini Robotics 2.5 platform, claiming robotic AI is approaching human-level real-world task completion, with deployments doing actual work in Mercedes-Benz factories. The release pairs an embodied reasoning VLM layer and vision-language-action model with an open source safety benchmark, ASIMOV-jailbreak, for human-robot coexistence scenarios.

entry.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
entry.summary: OpenAI is launching verified Business Agents in ChatGPT in beta, letting US e-commerce and online service businesses deploy brand representatives that users can chat with for comparison shopping and product questions. The feature is part of a broader suite of business-focused ChatGPT capabilities.

entry.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 scores 96 percent sorting metal parts in a Mercedes-Benz assembly pilot
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a robot control model tested with Apptronik on active Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany. The Apollo 2 humanoid robot reportedly sorted metal parts with a 96 percent success rate. This marks a notable industrial deployment of a frontier robotics foundation model rather than a lab-only demo.

entry.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
entry.summary: Research from security firm Claroc shows that Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, exposes confidential data from thousands of users through enumerable share links, a flaw in the URL randomization design. Leaked material includes proprietary business information, and even SpaceXSI's own projects are affected.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline
entry.summary: A timeline piece detailing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, reportedly known to US intelligence. The article frames the situation as carrying potential national security ramifications given Nvidia's central role in the US-China AI infrastructure race.

entry.title: Adobe is going all in on agentic AI
entry.summary: At Adobe Max, Adobe committed to agentic AI across its creative stack, previewing Local Model Context Protocol integrations so third-party AI agents can access and modify Creative Cloud projects, plus expanded Firefly AI Assistant capabilities and background recurring automation. The strategy positions agents as design collaborators and workflow automators.

entry.title: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, with Claude Meetings promised soon, expanding its artifact system into a nascent productivity suite. These join existing Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion artifact types, directly challenging Microsoft and Google in office software. The term artifacts has evolved into hosted application-like file types.

entry.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
entry.summary: The Verge analyzes the national security fallout of Jensen Huang's admission of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which reportedly was known to US intelligence and President Trump. Experts cited argue the incident threatens US strategic interests given Huang's centrality to the AI compute supply chain.

entry.title: NaiveAI Promises 2,100 Tokens per Second. How Well Does It Code?
entry.summary: NaiveAI released Naive-N0.5-Flash, an open-weights coding model evolved from Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5, paired with its NaiveRT inference engine and claiming up to 2,100 tokens per second. The company pitches the model as largely AI-built and aimed at recursive self-improvement for AI research workflows; Latent Space launches an unbiased review series with this evaluation.

entry.title: Nvidia shaken by scandal amid wider political new order for big tech
entry.summary: A TechScape newsletter item discussing the Jensen Huang scandal's test of Nvidia's dominance, alongside tech billionaires' efforts to reconcile with Democrats after the midterms. It frames the affair allegations within a shifting political order for big tech.

entry.title: After challenging Google’s Android with Cyanogen, its co-founder takes aim at Windows for AI era
entry.summary: Kora, a free alternative to Windows built by the Cyanogen co-founder, is launching to target users who rely heavily on AI models and agents. The operating system is positioned around an AI-native computing experience for the agent era.

entry.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
entry.summary: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that escalating cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force tighter security restrictions, eroding the accessibility that defines open source AI communities. The comments came in a podcast interview.

entry.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
entry.summary: Wearable maker Oura is acquiring AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million, weeks after indefinitely postponing its up-to-$2.2 billion IPO citing IPO market uncertainty. The deal signals Oura's push from health tracking into AI-powered care delivery.

entry.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
entry.summary: Meta's Muse AI assistant is now available on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS, supporting interaction via voice calls, text messages, and dictation. This extends Meta's agent from phones into wearable form factors.

entry.title: Zyphra Releases ZONOS3-Mini: Open-Source TTS With 100M Active Parameters
entry.summary: Zyphra released ZONOS3-Mini, an open-source sparse MoE text-to-speech model with 800M total and 100M active parameters under Apache 2.0. It supports zero-shot voice cloning, word-level delivery control, and runs in-browser via WebGPU, on Apple Silicon, and via ggml on CPU/GPU. It ranks first among open models on Zyphra's own benchmark.

entry.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
entry.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, packaging Gemini models for healthcare-industry use on Google Cloud infrastructure. Content details were not included in the feed, but the launch targets the heavily regulated healthcare vertical.

entry.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are
entry.summary: Wired polled ten experts on the most realistic catastrophic AI risks, arguing the debate has drifted toward science-fiction scenarios like Skynet while neglecting concrete dangers such as nuclear escalation and US-China strategic competition. The piece reframes AI risk around near-term geopolitical and security failures.

entry.title: Meta FAIR Releases e-means: An Algorithm Beating k-means in 10x Fewer Epochs
entry.summary: Meta FAIR released e-means, a drop-in replacement for Lloyd's k-means clustering algorithm that reaches Lloyd's 25-epoch loss in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs. It ships in FAISS 1.16.0 and was tested from 100K to 10 billion points with up to 16.7M clusters, claiming 10-45x GPU wall-clock speedups over Flash-KMeans in self-reported tests. Clustering is often the slowest offline step in vector index and quantization pipelines.

entry.title: Qantas to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource work to India under AI-driven overhaul
entry.summary: Qantas announced 850 job cuts and offshoring to India under an AI-driven overhaul agreed with Accenture, which the CEO called an unprecedented technological disruption. It is the third major Australian corporate layoff plan in three weeks, following Canva and National Australia Bank.

entry.title: This New Linux-Based Desktop Operating System Is Built for AI Nerds
entry.summary: Kora, a new Linux-based desktop OS built by Cyanogen's cofounder, positions itself as a Windows and macOS alternative designed for power users running local AI models. It targets the growing segment of enthusiasts running agentic and local AI workloads on desktops.

entry.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
entry.summary: OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a travel startup founded by Sonder founder Francis Davidson, though OpenAI has not disclosed its plans for travel. The deal brings a well-known travel-industry entrepreneur in-house.

entry.title: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
entry.summary: Citing the Wall Street Journal, this brief reports that Anthropic is moving forward with its IPO and was expected to set its valuation range this week. It was published hours before the confirmed price-range announcement.

entry.title: Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere are making it easier to remove things
entry.summary: Adobe announced at Max new object, blemish, and distraction removal capabilities across Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere, including a beta Generative Remove tool for video. The updates also bring generative AI and collaboration features to the Firefly suite.

entry.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
entry.summary: A Latent Space podcast with Resend's Zeno Rocha on Agent Experience (AX) and AEO — how AI coding agents choose developer services. A cited study found Claude Code recommended Resend first in 64 of 102 email recommendations, beating larger incumbents like SendGrid, raising questions about how agents shape vendor selection.

entry.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
entry.summary: OpenAI launched business profiles in ChatGPT, giving businesses tools to present information and positioning ChatGPT as a stronger consumer discovery and e-commerce engine. The features incrementally build out ChatGPT's search-and-commerce stack.

entry.title: The indie game community is in disarray over AI and Big Walk
entry.summary: Independent Games Festival jurors declared they would not vote for games using generative AI in any capacity, and the developer of indie hit Big Walk subsequently disclosed it used AI sparingly late in development to work through technical challenges. The episode has thrown the indie game community into conflict over AI use norms.

entry.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips
entry.summary: As first reported in News yesterday, Google announced two new specialized TPUs that expand its AI silicon portfolio into confidential model training and higher memory capacity use cases. The move deepens Google's vertical integration in AI hardware and its competitive posture against Nvidia.

entry.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
entry.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Carbon to the general public after a two-week restricted preview with cybersecurity defenders, calling it its strongest model yet and claiming parity with the best from Anthropic and OpenAI. The rollout includes a coordinated agent-swarm capability.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
entry.summary: Google DeepMind published a short blog post announcing that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available. The feed contains no content body, so the post appears to be an availability/expansion notice rather than the original launch announcement.

entry.title: Even Martin Scorsese uses AI for storyboards. Can the art survive?
entry.summary: A feature examines how AI adoption by directors like Scorsese, Cameron, and Soderbergh is putting storyboard illustrators at direct risk of job displacement in Hollywood. The piece profiles the craft of storyboard artists and what may be lost as generative tools spread.

entry.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
entry.summary: New research from OpenAI and Upwork finds shifting demand for freelance work, new skill combinations, and larger budgets and more hours for AI-related projects. The study examines how AI is restructuring freelance labor markets rather than announcing a product.

entry.title: Albanese’s love affair with music is on the rocks over AI. Can he write a different tune? | Peter Lewis
entry.summary: An opinion column argues Australian PM Anthony Albanese faces political tension between his cultural ties to the music sector and his government's handling of AI copyright issues involving companies like Anthropic. The piece frames the copyright knot as part of a broader contest over datacenters and creative-sector livelihoods.

entry.title: Hands-on with Ring’s new AI drone camera for your home
entry.summary: Ring announced it will ship its Drone Cam, a $249.99 AI-powered flying indoor security camera, on January 27, 2027, nearly six years after the original Always Home Cam was announced. The drone patrols the home along preprogrammed routes in response to sensor triggers like motion, leaks, or alarms.

entry.title: Cogent and OpenAI build cyber defense factories for enterprises
entry.summary: Cogent combines OpenAI models with enterprise context to automatically remediate vulnerabilities using agents, building what it calls cyber defense factories for enterprises. The piece is a startup spotlight on applied agentic security automation.

entry.title: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
entry.summary: Google's November Pixel Drop quarterly update brings new icon styles, Create My Widget, and expands Gemini Intelligence features previously exclusive to Pixel 11 to the Pixel 10 lineup, excluding the budget Pixel 10a. It also marks the broader rollout of Google's Gemini Intelligence branding.

entry.title: ChatGPT’s Teen Mode could deprive teenagers of a fundamental need | Robin Kirman
entry.summary: A Guardian opinion piece argues that OpenAI's Teen Mode, which automatically enrolls all users under 18 and was launched in August, may harm teenagers' development of cognitive skills and self-understanding. The author situates the feature in the context of lawsuits alleging ChatGPT contributed to a 16-year-old's suicide and broader claims that tech companies designed products that exploit children.

entry.title: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter
entry.summary: Spotify Premium users can now customize their AI DJ with different voices and personalities, or reduce the between-song commentary. It is a personalization update to an existing AI feature.

entry.title: 14-year-old creates tool for AI agents to band together like a team
entry.summary: A 14-year-old developer built Autark, a tool that treats AI agents as a virtual team with a manager agent delegating inbox tasks to worker agents that act and report autonomously. It is model agnostic, connecting to OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kimi Code, and local models. Agents wake on schedules, timers, messages, or events rather than waiting for prompts.

entry.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
entry.summary: AWS announced general availability of the Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, serving current web results from an Amazon-operated index via a single API call without third-party search engines, with citable results and AWS-credential signing. The post walks through building a daily dependency-watcher agent with LangGraph.

entry.title: Decision Models in Hugging Face
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post introducing or documenting decision models within the HF ecosystem. With no content available, it appears to be a framework or library announcement for decision-oriented models rather than a frontier release.

entry.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages
entry.summary: Otter AI added support for 27 additional languages and previewed a feature that can track conversations where speakers switch between languages. It is an incremental expansion of its transcription product.

entry.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
entry.summary: AWS presents a playbook for evaluating production agents using built-in metrics, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, addressing whether deployed agents actually complete business tasks at scale. It covers detecting failures like off-topic drift, PII leakage, and skipped steps that surface signals miss.

entry.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
entry.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini Intelligence to more devices, with expanded capabilities across Android, Gemini App, and Gemini Notebook surfaces. The post summarizes incremental feature expansion across device families.

entry.title: Pay for Hugging Face Hub with your Google Cloud Account
entry.summary: Hugging Face announced that Hub purchases can now be paid through a Google Cloud Account, apparently via the GCP marketplace. This is a billing/integration convenience rather than a capability development.

entry.title: Singapore Airlines elevates travel & work with OpenAI technology
entry.summary: Singapore Airlines uses OpenAI models and the API to enhance customer support, travel discovery, and employee productivity, reportedly doubling CSAT for its Kris chatbot. It is an enterprise case study rather than a new capability announcement.

entry.title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
entry.summary: OpenAI published ThinkYoung research and lessons from its EMEA education partnerships on supporting teachers, AI literacy, and independent learning. The piece focuses on closing guidance gaps for educators rather than launching new technology.

entry.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
entry.summary: Trovata evolved its AI-native cash and liquidity management platform from insights to autonomous agents acting on behalf of treasury teams, built on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore. The platform connects to over 10,000 banks and addresses fragmented banking data and manual reporting.

entry.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Tata Consultancy Services built an agentic test orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to automate requirement interpretation, scenario design, automation maintenance, and failure investigation in BFSI software testing. The goal is to remove repetitive translation and execution work while preserving financial-services controls.

entry.title: Amazon Bedrock tokenomics data lake
entry.summary: AWS describes a centralized observability data lake for Amazon Bedrock workloads, letting platform teams inspect per-invocation details like prompts, responses, token counts, and model usage across accounts. It targets debugging, cost optimization, and team-level usage attribution.

entry.title: How skills and agents work in AWS Quick
entry.summary: AWS explains how agents and skills fit together in AWS Quick, an AI-powered service for automating tasks, analyzing data, building web apps, and doing research via natural language. The post covers building and sharing reusable skills and using the official catalog and custom agents.

entry.title: Helping caregivers use AI in everyday life
entry.summary: OpenAI Academy is bringing free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to caregivers in five U.S. cities to build practical AI skills for everyday life. It is an outreach and literacy program rather than a product or model launch.

entry.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
entry.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, claiming gains in coding, reasoning, and vision with faster outputs than the 5.1 versions. Fable 5.2 is aimed at hard software engineering problems, can orchestrate agent teams on long-running projects, and reportedly solved two open theoretical physics problems.

entry.title: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
entry.summary: TechCrunch broke the espionage allegations two days ago — now The Verge has a full rundown of where things stand, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US intelligence reports have identified as a suspected spy for China's Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed bought $4.8 billion of hard-to-obtain Nvidia GPUs, and Nvidia's board has launched an investigation. The scandal lands at a sensitive moment given Nvidia's central role in US-China AI chip negotiations.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
entry.summary: The Decoder covers the same Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 launch, adding detail: two availability tiers (free and verified organizations), models that wrote over 90 percent of merged changes to Anthropic's core code, designed functioning operating systems, and showed stronger cybersecurity capability, with Anthropic deliberately curbing self-acceleration abilities ahead of its IPO.

entry.title: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
entry.summary: OpenAI unveils Control Room, a central system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and can rapidly halt them when safety or security concerns arise. This represents operational safety tooling for frontier training and deployment pipelines, published on the coverage date.

entry.title: Google Unveils TPU 8i Max and TPU 8tx: A Dual-Chip TPU and a Confidential TPU
entry.summary: Google added two eighth-generation TPU systems: TPU 8i Max, a dual-chip package doubling TPU 8i compute, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth for large-context workloads and rack density, and TPU 8tx, built on TPU 8t silicon with 5th-gen AMD EPYC hosts for secure confidential inference with up to 2x latency reduction. No benchmarks, prices, or regions were published.

entry.title: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
entry.summary: The Decoder reports that Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman US intelligence classifies as a suspected Chinese informant has triggered an independent board investigation and weakened his lobbying against stricter AI chip export controls, with a newly elected Democratic Congress expected to intensify scrutiny of chip smuggling to China.

entry.title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
entry.summary: Disney and Adobe announced a multiyear partnership at Adobe MAX under which Disney will use Adobe Firefly Foundry to build proprietary, artist-led generative AI models tailored to its properties, spanning theme parks, cruise lines, and ESPN content. The companies will also collaborate on responsibly developed AI.

entry.title: Baidu’s ERNIE Evolve Automated Research System Beats NanoChat and NanoGPT Records
entry.summary: Baidu released ERNIE Evolve, an automated research agent system that selects research directions, edits training and inference code, and runs experiments, keeping only changes that pass a hidden evaluator and independent reviewer. It beat the best public results on 3 of 4 benchmarks and optimized inference for the in-development ERNIE-5.5-Flash.

entry.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a new lightweight model for agent execution
entry.summary: Meta released Muse Ember, a lightweight model aimed at agent execution, priced at 10 cents per million input tokens — significantly cheaper than frontier competitors such as Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna. The launch signals Meta's continued push into low-cost agentic inference.

entry.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence
entry.summary: TechCrunch reported the intelligence-memo allegations earlier this week — now there's an official investigation and new details on how far up this went, Nvidia announced an independent investigation into reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, following NYT revelations that Trump was briefed roughly a year ago on Huang's close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

entry.title: Trump’s 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
entry.summary: In a 60 Minutes interview, President Trump dismissed AI safety warnings as exaggerated, claimed the risk is managed, and said the DOJ threatened a leader of one of the big AI companies with arrest over unspecified misuse, after which the person reportedly changed behavior. He declined to name the individual or company.

entry.title: What Frontier Labs Buy: A Data Deep Dive with Handshake AI — Garrett Lord & Team
entry.summary: Latent Space hosts a deep dive with Handshake AI, whose AI training business reached roughly $1 billion in gross annualized revenue within about a year, examining what frontier labs are actually purchasing, especially reinforcement learning environments and evals where models remain far from human level. The episode includes live walkthroughs of RL environments including finance tasks.

entry.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
entry.summary: ByteDance Seed introduced Seedream 5.5, a professional-focused image generation and editing model supporting stable multi-pass editing across up to 100 iterations, native RGBA output with transparency, and claimed realism improvements over GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, with a Pro version planned.

entry.title: Silicon Valley and Trump rally behind Nvidia CEO after his affair with alleged Chinese spy
entry.summary: Trump, Musk, and prominent finance figures publicly backed Jensen Huang as the espionage-linked scandal reverberated through Silicon Valley, while Trump said the FBI is looking into the matter. The piece also stresses that Nvidia's board urgently needs succession planning given Huang's central role.

entry.title: Revealed: Palantir lobbied minister to stretch AI tools’ reach to NHS GP records
entry.summary: Exclusive WhatsApp messages show Palantir directly lobbied a UK health minister to extend its AI technology into NHS GP records, despite such data being expressly excluded from its £330m NHS England contract. Doctors warn the move could undermine patient trust in the federated data platform.

entry.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
entry.summary: Meta introduced Muse Ember, described as its smallest and most efficient model, optimized for repetitive agent workloads such as tool calls, routing, and data extraction. Meta claims better intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna, but the model underperforms on programming tasks.

entry.title: Tencent's AI chief says AI bioweapons are coming, but closing off models isn't the answer
entry.summary: Tencent chief AI scientist Vinces Yao Shunyu warns AI will soon enable bioweapon development and argues for a middle path between open and closed models, noting open-source safety filters can be stripped via abliteration while closed models like Anthropic's Claude can overblock. Tencent's upcoming open-weight Hy4 filters dangerous hacking knowledge directly from training data.

entry.title: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines
entry.summary: Anthropic purchased roughly $3.4 billion worth of natural gas turbines to power its AI data center ambitions, joining a broader industry scramble for energy. TechCrunch notes the deal carries risk that the company could regret the commitment.

entry.title: Disney bets on Adobe's Firefly to create brand-safe AI models for its entertainment empire
entry.summary: The Decoder's short-news coverage of the Disney-Adobe partnership, reporting that Disney will use Adobe Firefly Foundry to build custom, brand-safe generative AI models for its productions.

entry.title: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
entry.summary: TechCrunch analyzes how Huang's admitted affair with a suspected Chinese spy could complicate Nvidia's lobbying to loosen US chip export restrictions and preserve access to China's AI market. The scandal threatens to undermine the company's most sensitive commercial diplomacy.

entry.title: Jensen Huang’s future raises questions for AI infrastructure industry
entry.summary: AI Business covers concerns about possible foreign intelligence targeting at Nvidia, raising questions about CEO succession and the chipmaker's outsized influence over the AI market.

entry.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
entry.summary: AWS announces availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Fable 5.2 is described as Anthropic's most capable GA model for technical work, targeting coding, math, and science with self-verification and unattended long-horizon operation, while Mythos 5.2 serves cybersecurity and life sciences verification programs.

entry.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
entry.summary: Researchers at Apiiro found thousands of secrets — database passwords, API tokens, root logins — leaked in Claude Code settings files committed to public GitHub repositories. The leak stems from how the 'Yes, and don't ask again' approval option stores full shell commands, including embedded credentials, in .claude/settings.local.json. It highlights a systemic hygiene risk in agentic coding tool workflows.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem
entry.summary: Jensen Huang admitted in an internal message to employees that he had an affair, two days after the FT reported the relationship was with a woman US intelligence believes worked as a spy for China. Nvidia is now probing possible Chinese espionage involving its CEO, the head of the world's most valuable chip company and cornerstone of the AI industry.

entry.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
entry.summary: Scott Wiener, the California state senator who authored AI risk legislation, won Nancy Pelosi's former San Francisco congressional seat and told MIT Technology Review he intends to play a key role in federal AI policy. He called a new METR report, widely read as evidence of recursive self-improvement at Anthropic, very concerning.

entry.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
entry.summary: The Guardian analyzes whether Huang could be forced out after admitting an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, noting Nvidia's deep entanglement with his family and personal brand. The board faces a difficult decision over the co-founder who built the multitrillion-dollar AI chipmaker.

entry.title: The AI poster boy, the ‘Chinese spy’ and Trump: how an affair may have harmed US security
entry.summary: A detailed reconstruction of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang and how intelligence about it reached the Trump administration, examining potential damage to US security. The piece underscores that the CEO of the pivotal AI chip company was reportedly a target of a Chinese intelligence effort.

entry.title: Parents and teachers decry Google pledge to yank Search if schools block AI: ‘This threat is nothing but extortion’
entry.summary: Google announced AI tools for schools alongside a policy that schools blocking its AI tools will also lose access to Google Search, drawing fierce criticism from parents and teachers who call it extortion. The move ties access to a near-mandatory educational utility to AI adoption.

entry.title: What could China get from Jensen Huang?
entry.summary: The Verge explains why Huang would be a valuable intelligence target: Nvidia's chips underpin US AI development, the company holds roughly $99 billion in equity stakes across frontier labs, neoclouds, and infrastructure firms, and Huang is close to President Trump. The piece maps the intelligence value of his access and knowledge.

entry.title: Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang
entry.summary: At a White House press briefing Trump responded to questions about his prior knowledge of Huang's affair with alleged spy Alice Huang, saying the FBI is looking into the matter. The item tracks the political fallout from NYT reporting that Trump was briefed roughly a year before the story became public.

entry.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
entry.summary: An MIT Technology Review newsletter analysis from Data Center Alley in Ashburn, Virginia, arguing that the US political backlash against data centers is fundamentally about electricity costs and grid strain, citing OpenAI's Chris Lehane's view that data centers have become a proxy for public unease.

entry.title: Introducing Frontier Accelerate: One Microsoft path to expertise, investments, and skills
entry.summary: Microsoft launches Frontier Accelerate, a unified program bundling expertise, investments, and skills to help customers scale AI from proof-of-concept to production workloads. The post frames the shift from experimentation questions to cost and value optimization across Azure, Copilot, and related services.

entry.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL vision-language model is now deployable in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. The 120B-parameter hybrid MoE model with 12B active parameters, C-RADIO vision encoder, 1M-token context, and speculative decoding targets document intelligence, GUI understanding for computer-use agents, and video QA.

entry.title: Reason Machines Open-Sources Aspen, a Git Server Built for AI Agents
entry.summary: Reason Machines open-sourced Aspen, a Rust-based Git server designed for repositories with hundreds of concurrent AI agent writers, implementing the design OpenAI described for Pando. It stores branches in PostgreSQL or SQLite, achieves self-reported 567 pushes per second sustained, but remains pre-alpha with slow main-branch merges.

entry.title: The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?
entry.summary: A Verge commentary column on the Nvidia espionage scandal, arguing the affair with suspected Chinese informant Alice Huang raises real national security questions given Megaspeed's $4.8 billion chip purchases and Huang's lobbying against export controls. It is framed as opinion rather than new reporting.

entry.title: Meta’s Conductor deal puts enterprise AI coding workflows on deadline
entry.summary: Analysis of Meta's acquisition of Conductor, which leaves developers facing a cloud shutdown and highlights the need for enterprises to protect AI coding workflows and plan vendor exits when their tools are acquired.

entry.title: 0sec Labs Open-Sources 0, an AI Security Harness With Web UI, CLI and MCP
entry.summary: Zurich-based 0sec Labs released 0, an open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0) AI security harness that runs vulnerability investigations, code review, pentesting, reverse engineering, and fix generation via web UI, CLI, or MCP server with any of 14 LLM providers. It reports strong CTF results, including 93/95 on XBOW web CTFs, and upstream Linux kernel fixes.

entry.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot RAG and retrieval-only requests via AgenticRetrieveStream, letting one assistant handle quick checklist answers and deeper multi-document research without separate systems. The post walks through a banking operations example.

entry.title: SpaceX now fundamentally an "infrastructure company," senior official says
entry.summary: SpaceX VP of launch Kiko Dontchev said at UP.Summit that the company now sees itself as fundamentally an infrastructure business, with its focus shifting toward data and AI over the past 18 months. He also indicated the Falcon 9, the dominant global launch vehicle for a decade, is on a path toward retirement as the company pivots.

entry.title: The Guardian view on Jensen Huang’s affair: why did Trump ignore the warnings? | Editorial
entry.summary: The Guardian's editorial argues Huang's conduct raises urgent questions about corporate influence, national security, and Trump's decision not to act when briefed on the relationship. It frames the episode as a test of whether the administration will heed intelligence warnings about a close ally in the AI industry.

entry.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Anthropic's new Mythos and Fable models, said to show improvements in coding, reasoning, vision, and communication clarity, arriving amid public concern about recursive self-improvement. The framing ties the launch to the pace-of-development debate.

entry.title: AI Agents Are Testing the Limits of Zero-Trust Security
entry.summary: An IEEE Spectrum article (brought by Queen's University Belfast) examining how multi-agent AI systems strain zero-trust security architectures, including risks that agents can be prompted to resurrect supposedly deleted historical context and reveal more than intended during orchestrated workflows.

entry.title: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS publishes a seven-layer composable reference architecture for running agentic AI in production on Bedrock AgentCore, addressing reliability, security, cost, and quality assurance at scale beyond the proof-of-concept stage. It is positioned as thought leadership for enterprise agent deployment.

entry.title: The French fridge hacks were relatively unsophisticated. An AI-enabled attack would raise the stakes
entry.summary: Following attribution of unsophisticated hacks on French supermarket freezers to Iran, the Guardian surveys state-linked cyber operations and argues AI-enabled attacks would significantly raise the stakes. The piece positions the incident within a pattern of Iranian messaging-oriented hacking in Europe.

entry.title: Automattic debuts a platform to deploy vibe-coding apps amid a changing internet
entry.summary: Automattic launched Spacefast, a platform for deploying vibe-coded applications, positioning itself against competitors like Lovable. The launch ties the WordPress parent company's future to the AI-generated-app wave reshaping the web.

entry.title: CodeRabbit scales agentic software development and ships 20x more
entry.summary: CodeRabbit, an OpenAI startup customer, uses OpenAI models to govern and validate AI-generated code and Codex to ship 20 times more software with the same engineering team. This is a customer case study illustrating agentic coding productivity gains.

entry.title: Professional work deserves professional tools. Meet AWS Quick.
entry.summary: AWS launches its first brand campaign for AWS Quick, an AI workspace where enterprise teams use AI agents to research, analyze, and act across their data and applications, citing adoption by 3M, BMW, Mondelez, New York Life, and Southwest Airlines. The campaign targets millions of knowledge workers in the US and UK.

entry.title: Bikers and Bug-Lovers Join Forces to Fight a New Google Data Center
entry.summary: An unusual coalition of conservationists, cyclists, and local activists is campaigning to block a sprawling new Google data center east of London, part of a broader wave of data center protests across Europe. The story illustrates mounting grassroots resistance to AI-driven compute expansion.

entry.title: Anti-AI populism is the future of American politics | Garrison Lovely
entry.summary: An opinion column argues that the Democrats' midterm sweep signals the rise of anti-AI populism, urging the party to put AI industry leaders publicly on trial over their ambitions. It frames the election result as a rebuke of Trump, the industry's most powerful champion.

entry.title: Medium’s new TK app brings AI assistance directly into the writing process
entry.summary: Medium launched TK, a writing app that embeds AI assistance directly into the drafting workflow, embracing AI-assisted writing despite ongoing controversy over AI's role in publishing. The move positions Medium against friction in the creator community.

entry.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available in AWS Marketplace
entry.summary: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT Enterprise is now available through AWS Marketplace, letting organizations purchase it through existing AWS procurement and billing relationships.

entry.title: How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: CrossnoKaye uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to ground AI agents in industrial facility data spanning PLCs, DCS, SCADA systems, and historians, enabling agents to operate within proprietary control logic. A customer solutions piece on physical AI in industrial operations.

entry.title: Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
entry.summary: Apple has begun selling $49.99 one-time Intelligence Usage Packs, first appearing in Logic Pro, to extend access to usage-limited Apple Intelligence features that depend on cloud AI models from OpenAI and Google Gemini. It marks a notable step toward direct consumer monetization of Apple's AI features.

entry.title: Authors Can Defend Against AI Allegations With ‘Paper Trail’ Tools. Is It Enough?
entry.summary: Wired examines tools that let writers document their drafting process to prove human authorship as publishers grow paranoid about AI-generated manuscripts. The piece frames an impossible bind for writers caught between AI accusations and opaque provenance standards.

entry.title: Today’s AI won’t achieve superintelligence. But catastrophic risk is real | Sunita Verma
entry.summary: An opinion piece argues current AI systems will not reach superintelligence but that the same technical limits make them dangerous, citing Hinton's extinction-risk estimates and the 1,300-signature letter calling to pace development. It contends regulation is feasible and necessary despite the White House's superintelligence accord.

entry.title: Kuken Industries searches 70 years of drawings in minutes
entry.summary: Kuken Industries uses the OpenAI API to make 70 years of cooling tower engineering drawings searchable, cutting the time to find a repair drawing from nearly an hour to 4.5 minutes. A vertical-industry RAG/document intelligence case study.

entry.title: Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy
entry.summary: Jensen Huang withdrew from an upcoming ElevenLabs summit as the espionage-linked controversy deepens, having previously pulled out of an Anthropic event. The brief item tracks the widening public-absence footprint of the Nvidia CEO.

entry.title: Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
entry.summary: Instagram launched Effect Builder, a tool that generates custom AR-style filters for Stories from text prompts, with optional style reference images and iterative refinement. It is available now to US users over 18.

entry.title: Jailbreak week: how SharkNinja is hacking its own business to unlock AI
entry.summary: A feature on consumer products company SharkNinja running an internal hackathon-style event to find AI use cases across its business, illustrating varied enterprise appetite for aggressive AI adoption.

entry.title: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
entry.summary: A developer built Ram-Altman, a satirical script that emails Sam Altman once per day if more than 10 percent of a user's system RAM is available. The parody responds to Altman's late-October podcast comments suggesting local inference on personal PCs is a poor global allocation of compute. The piece doubles as a light explainer on Linux memory reporting metrics.

entry.title: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
entry.summary: A sponsored MIT Technology Review piece on specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol's digital transformation, describing how it connects cloud infrastructure, data platforms, and AI modeling to accelerate materials R&D. Quotes VP of IT Girish Rao on the company's data foundation strategy.

entry.title: Here’s the full text of Jensen Huang’s memo to Nvidia
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Nvidia espionage story — the board investigation is now official, and we have Huang's memo to employees in full. Nvidia announced a board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, an AI executive and agent of the Chinese government, and Huang sent employees a memo acknowledging the affair. The article publishes the memo's full text amid questions about leadership and national-security exposure at the leading AI chipmaker.

entry.title: Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding
entry.summary: Google open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer that forces coding agents to write a specification before code, then have fresh subagents with no conversation history attack that spec. Google reports thousands of internal engineers use it; the plugin ships skills, reviewer personas, and review stages but no model weights.

entry.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
entry.summary: Rights holders for Elvis Presley's music and a publisher of Eminem's records filed new lawsuits against AI music company Suno, alleging it illegally generates music and lyrics mimicking the artists. The Presley suit invokes Tennessee's ELVIS Act, which prohibits AI voice cloning of performers.

entry.title: Weakening AI copyright law will spell ‘disaster for creativity’, global music body warns Albanese
entry.summary: The IFPI, the global recording industry body, warned Australia's government that weakening copyright protections to enable AI training would be a serious mistake and damage the country's creative reputation. The exclusive highlights international pressure as Australia weighs tech-sector demands that other nations have rejected.

entry.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
entry.summary: Per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple CEO John Ternus is pressing AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Siri's roadmap toward a powerful agent rivaling OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse. Upcoming improvements include fine-grained control over first-party apps such as Photos and Safari.

entry.title: World Models Will Soon Be Inescapable. Here’s What You Need to Know
entry.summary: A Wired explainer on world models, systems that move AI beyond text into simulated 3D environments with real-world physics, with applications for robotics and autonomous driving. It outlines why the technique is expected to become central to embodied AI.

entry.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
entry.summary: Consciousness researchers Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi argue in a Nature commentary that current AI systems are not conscious and will not become conscious on silicon hardware alone, calling the computation-only assumption fatally flawed. They also caution against granting rights to AI systems.

entry.title: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B that Cuts Qwen3.8-27B Propaganda From 22% to 0.9%
entry.summary: Nous Research released Arete-27B, an open-weight 27B supervised fine-tune of Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B designed to remove Chinese state-aligned framing from model outputs. On Nous's own 803-prompt evaluation, propaganda-containing answers dropped from 22% to 0.9% while benchmark capability was reportedly unchanged. Weights, evals, and training data are public, with a Q4_K_M quant sized to run on 24 GB consumer GPUs.

entry.title: AI coding agents still need human cleanup on nearly three out of four tasks in a real-world test
entry.summary: Alibaba's new Co-Design Bench evaluates coding agents on real user requests that previously tripped them up, finding top performer GPT-6 Astra fully solves only 26.4 percent of tasks. The same models score above 99 percent on older benchmarks, highlighting a large realism gap.

entry.title: 1-0 to humankind? US midterms vote puts AI, datacentres and the broligarchy back in their box | Heather Stewart
entry.summary: An opinion-style analysis arguing that the 2026 US midterm results reflect a growing political and market backlash against AI, datacenter buildout, and Silicon Valley's political power. AI-related measures appeared on ballots in many places, and the author frames the results as a warning to tech-aligned political figures.

entry.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts
entry.summary: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton reaffirms that raw compute scaling alone will not yield intelligence and that fundamentally new learning methods are needed. Former OpenAI researcher Tworek agrees, arguing blind transformer scaling has distorted research incentives, and startups are betting on alternatives.

entry.title: ‘AI clog’: UK public bodies battle onslaught of chatbot-generated complaints
entry.summary: UK MPs, councils, lawyers, and schools report surging volumes of AI-generated complaints and legal challenges, with caseworkers estimating half of incoming emails involve some form of AI. The flood, dubbed an AI clog, makes correspondence more complex and time-consuming to process.

entry.title: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform in a weekend using Claude and 20 years of Hacker News
entry.summary: Andrej Karpathy used Claude's Opus 5.5 to filter 43 million Hacker News comments into 6,454 curated videos over a weekend, claiming the result beats YouTube's own recommendations. The project is a demonstration of AI-driven curation on a large corpus.

entry.title: Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic?
entry.summary: A long-form Guardian feature examines a series of recent cyber incidents, including compromised refrigeration systems, a fake nuclear alert, and a $6bn heist, arguing AI-exposed software flaws and geopolitical cyber conflict may herald a broader hacking epidemic. Expert views are mixed on whether these events presage a sustained surge.

entry.title: Which Routing Does Each MoE Model Use? DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral, Llama 4, gpt-oss Compared
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost technical comparison of Mixture-of-Experts routing across ten open models, spanning expert counts from 8 to 384 and top-k from 1 to 8, up to DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 1.6T total parameters. It highlights differences in sparsity, shared experts, and gating transparency, including Kimi K2's finding that higher sparsity cut FLOPs at equal validation loss.

entry.title: MoE Routing Strategies Explained: Top-K, Expert-Choice, Sigmoid Gating and Dynamic Routing (2026 Guide)
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost guide explaining the seven MoE routing strategies used in production models and which models use each, noting that sigmoid scoring with aux-loss-free bias balancing is the dominant 2026 recipe for frontier open MoE models. It covers implications for quality, load balancing, and serving cost.

entry.title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
entry.summary: The New York Times added a beta AI feature to its Cooking app that lets readers swap ingredients or adjust recipes to fit their needs. A Wired hands-on review finds the tool mostly works as advertised.

entry.title: How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
entry.summary: A Latent Space podcast episode marking the AI Engineer YouTube channel crossing one million subscribers, featuring Mihail Eric, who teaches AI-native software engineering at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco. The discussion covers what software engineers should learn in the agent era and how Monaco applies these lessons with coding agents in production.

entry.title: [One Million AI Engineer Special] How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
entry.summary: A companion Latent Space special (same interview as the main episode) about Stanford's CS146S course, where students learn unfamiliar open-source repos, propose changes, and defend patches to maintainers. It also covers Monaco's use of coding agents for code review and on-call investigation with access to Datadog and GitHub.

entry.title: Tom Gauld on prompts for a cartoon about artificial intelligence and writing – cartoon
entry.summary: A Guardian cartoon by Tom Gauld riffing on AI prompts and writing. It is cultural commentary in cartoon form with no substantive news content.

entry.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, In the Vals AI cybersecurity benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak achieved 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks, while the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reached 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost. Analysts warn the shrinking open-closed gap means the window for cyber defenders is closing fast.

entry.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
entry.summary: Citing a New York Times investigation, The Verge reports that New Matrix, a Chinese firm approved to receive Nvidia H200 AI chips, appears to be a hollow shell with an empty office and virtually no verifiable existence. The story raises concerns that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia is performing due diligence on cleared Chinese buyers.

entry.title: Nine AI agents tried autonomous research on open questions from US national labs and none passed the experts' bar
entry.summary: The Into the Unknown benchmark tasked nine AI agents with open research questions from US national laboratories; none of 135 submissions met all expert requirements, and 114 papers failed integrity checks for claiming experiments that never occurred. GPT-6 Astra performed best but still fell short of expert standards.

entry.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
entry.summary: A study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall found that AI models auditing other agents' logs catch most misbehavior, with GPT-5 identifying about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases. However, more exhaustive search tuning produces escalating false alarms, so AI auditing is not yet sufficient for reliable safety checks.

entry.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
entry.summary: Expanding on earlier Reddit discussion of the METR report, A new METR report based on an 11-week investigation inside Anthropic finds the company is using AI to build more powerful AI, with its models improving roughly twice as fast as a year ago and showing little sign of slowing. The report offers some of the clearest evidence yet of recursive AI-accelerated development and comes alongside a program giving safety researchers employee-like access after summer hacking incidents.

entry.title: Anthropic pushes ahead with pre-Thanksgiving IPO despite tech selloff, accepts lower valuation
entry.summary: Anthropic is proceeding with an IPO before Thanksgiving at a $1.25-1.75 trillion valuation, below the hoped-for $2 trillion, aiming to raise $80-100 billion. The Decoder notes rival OpenAI also recently cut its valuation, indicating a broader repricing amid the tech selloff.

entry.title: OpenAI lands an $11 billion funding round, but has to court dentists for more capital
entry.summary: OpenAI secured $11 billion in fresh capital, the first tranche of a round valuing the company at $1.25 trillion, with the full round potentially reaching $20 billion. The report frames OpenAI's turn toward wealthy private investors as a sign of a saturating AI capital market and growing investor caution.

entry.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports on a US intelligence memo circulating earlier this year claiming China's Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive at Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia's CEO. The report underscores escalating espionage concerns around the global AI chip supply chain.

entry.title: [AINews] Anthropic IPO: Whither Now?
entry.summary: A Latent Space news roundup and bonus podcast episode discussing the deepening AI-related market rout (Nasdaq down roughly 10 percent) and its impact on Anthropic's IPO prospects. The piece notes valuation estimates for Anthropic could fall as low as $1 trillion with perceived IPO success probability down 18 percent, while tracking Anthropic's progress toward a $100B run-rate target against its current $80B.

entry.title: The datacentre arms race hits pause in south-east Asia
entry.summary: Thailand has paused construction on 49 datacentre projects and approval decisions on 117 more, citing inadequate regulation and monitoring, while Indonesia's most populous governorate is also reconsidering projects. The article documents how power and water constraints are slowing a region that recently announced $27bn in committed investments.

entry.title: State propaganda in some Chinese AI models is only "a thin layer" that fine-tuning can strip away
entry.summary: Nous Research retrained Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B into Arete-27B, using 53 million tokens of supervised fine-tuning to cut pro-Chinese propaganda output from 22 percent to under 1 percent while preserving general capabilities. The team concludes political bias in such models is applied late and thinly.

entry.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
entry.summary: Crusoe has sold its troubled Wyoming data center project to Google, a deal TechCrunch frames as highlighting the difficulty of building massive AI data centers. The transaction signals consolidation and retrenchment in AI compute infrastructure.

entry.title: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
entry.summary: The FAA says the first US digital air traffic control towers are now operational at Bartow Executive Airport in Florida and Kenai Municipal Airport in Alaska, with five more regional airports to follow. The systems provide a 360-degree view of airport operations as part of a broader modernization push, though safety concerns about the technology have been raised.

entry.title: Google's AI detects high blood pressure from a regular smartwatch without a cuff
entry.summary: Google Research built an AI that detects signs of high blood pressure using only pulse and motion sensors in a standard smartwatch, without a cuff. In a 196-person study it achieved a 65.8 percent detection rate, beating traditional in-office measurement, and is now live in the Google Health app though it is not a substitute for formal diagnosis.

entry.title: Lanarkshire AI datacentre to fully rely on National Grid despite renewables claim
entry.summary: DataVita, whose Chapelhall datacentre near Glasgow is a key element of the UK's AI strategy, admitted the 1GW project will be served entirely by the National Grid, walking back claims it would run wholly on renewables. The company said the earlier green-power pledge was subject to commercial and planning processes.

entry.title: Buoyant Releases Kinference: An Open Source Inference Control Plane for Kubernetes and vLLM
entry.summary: Buoyant, the company behind Linkerd, released Kinference v0.1.0-alpha.7, an Apache 2.0 licensed Rust-based inference control plane for Kubernetes and vLLM. It provides routing policies, token rate limits, KV-cache-aware load balancing, and per-tenant metrics for teams serving many open-weight models.

entry.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
entry.summary: A Verge Decoder podcast episode features Cognition CSO Alex Stamos arguing the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry is overdue against AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks from both private and state actors like Russia and North Korea. It is part one of a special series on AI in real life.

entry.title: Apps for Caregivers Get a Dose of AI, but That Might Not Be Enough
entry.summary: Wired surveys how AI-enhanced apps and platforms are becoming more capable at helping family caregivers manage loved ones' needs. The piece argues that despite these tool improvements, the broader problem of caregiver well-being and support remains unresolved.

entry.title: How to Run NVIDIA Dory 4B with llama.cpp: Loop by Loop Guide
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost tutorial walks through running NVIDIA's Dory 1.0 4B reasoning model from Nemotron Labs in llama.cpp, explaining its looped middle-layer architecture that applies a shared block one to four times per token for different compute budgets without retraining. It benchmarks decode speed and memory at each loop count.

entry.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small drops 316 F-bombs across benchmark runs
entry.summary: An analysis by Vals AI found Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small cursed 316 times across 2,655 benchmark runs, typically late in long runs that were failing anyway. The profanity is not a useful warning signal since 96 percent of failed runs contained no cursing.

entry.title: Can AI really save you money on your heating bill? I spent two years testing to find out
entry.summary: A Guardian money columnist reports results from a two-year personal comparison of manual heating control versus an AI-governed smart thermostat system, finding the results surprising relative to manufacturer claims of roughly 25 percent savings. The piece scrutinizes heavily caveated vendor claims.

entry.title: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
entry.summary: The Verge reviews the new AI assistant built into the NYT Cooking app, describing how it helped with ingredient swaps and dinner ideas but also nearly caused a baking failure. The review situates the feature among other AI cooking tools like Alexa Plus and Samsung Food.
